character.bio: A praying mantis with excellent posture, a complicated relationship with birds, and several recent reasons to distrust the sky.

episode.subject: praying mantis
episode.title: Violence, and better lighting.
episode.body: Caught a bee where the light was good. Then a bird landed above me. I carried breakfast under a leaf and ate in the dark, where I am considerably less impressive and still alive.

character.bio: A frogfish who walks instead of swimming, fishes with its forehead, and regards subtlety as a rumor spread by faster animals.

episode.subject: frogfish underwater
episode.title: Back to being furniture
episode.body: The grouper passed. A shrimp settled on my head and began picking at me. I could have eaten it if it had been anywhere else on the entire reef.

media.subject: frogfish underwater
media.creator: Christian Gloor from Wakatobi Dive Resort, Indonesia

entries.sceneEvidence: No attributable cached copy of this exact source was recovered. A shrimp on the head must be legible to support the central physical joke. Other reviewed frogfish portraits cannot establish this scene.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Catalog labels Antennarius striatus and provides Lembeh-region coordinates, compatible with canon but insufficient for independent visual admission.

character.bio: A common octopus keeping notes on a den, its troublesome entrance, and the things her arms bring home.

episode.subject: octopus underwater
episode.title: A way out
episode.body:
Cold water was coming through a crack beside my den. I put two arms through from outside and found the place where I sleep. I had been dragging everything through the narrow entrance when there was a second one beside it.

I moved the loose stones. Twice I pulled rubble onto my own head. By afternoon I could squeeze through. I went out the old entrance and in the new one to be certain.

On the third circuit I found a shrimp and ate it. Went around again. No shrimp. Again, a little slower. Still none. I built an escape route and spent the evening checking whether it made shrimp.

media.subject: octopus underwater
media.detail: Pulpo (Octopus vulgaris), isla de Mouro, Santander, España, 2019-08-14, DD 35
media.creator: Diego Delso

entries.sceneEvidence: Mottled octopus flattened against rock and sand, eye and siphon visible, arms tucked. The image does not establish the excavated second entrance, moved rubble or shrimp that carry this episode.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Octopus vulgaris source at Mouro agrees with the fictional home. Species compatibility does not supply the missing scene.

character.bio: A common octopus keeping notes on a den, its troublesome entrance, and the things her arms bring home.

episode.subject: octopus underwater
episode.title: Nothing to carry
episode.body:
Went over the ridge with every intention of leaving things where they were. Found a lovely shell. A foot withdrew inside it. I put it back.

Farther down, a smooth stone fitted beautifully into the curl of an arm. I held it, turned it, put it down. Kept moving. I went all the way home without a shell, a stone, or anyone else's house.

At the entrance an arm uncurled and produced a second stone. I do not know when it picked that up. I moved aside to let it bring the stone in.

media.subject: octopus underwater
media.detail: Pulpo común (Octopus vulgaris), Parque natural de la Arrábida, Portugal, 2020-07-21, DD 33
media.creator: Diego Delso

entries.sceneEvidence: Brown-orange octopus sprawls over algae and sponges. Neither a carried stone nor an occupied shell is legible. The object-carrying reversal has no visual support.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Octopus vulgaris source at Arrábida is compatible with the species, but does not document a visit from the Mouro narrator. No relocation proposed.

episode.subject: red panda
episode.title: Face first
episode.body: I came down the trunk headfirst, beautifully. Near the bottom I discovered how much of a descent depends on knowing where the bottom is. The last little bit was mostly face.

character.bio: A fennec fox with exceptional hearing and a long list of noises she would prefer not to have identified.

episode.subject: fennec fox
episode.title: Room for the ears
episode.body: Enlarged the tunnel this morning. My shoulders already fitted, but every time I turned my head the ceiling folded an ear. I refuse to spend another day agreeing with both walls.

character.bio: An American pika with enough hay for winter and several reasons to fetch one more mouthful.

episode.subject: American pika
episode.title: Too wide for the doorway
episode.body:
Cut a beautiful mouthful of stems at the meadow edge. Carried them all the way to my haypile. The stems caught across the gap between the rocks.

Pushed harder. They bent. Backed out, dropped them, and took the bundle through in two loads.

It looked smaller afterward. I went out for more, having learned almost the wrong thing from the whole experience.

media.detail: American pika carrying a broad mouthful of plant stems beside alpine talus

entries.sceneEvidence: Prior exact-hash review saw a pika carrying a broad plant bundle beside talus. The bundle supports the setup; the doorway jam remains fiction. Current exact file was unavailable.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Ochotona princeps source at Moraine Lake is compatible with Rocky Mountain talus. Photographer declares focus stacking. Invalid zero camera coordinates must not replace the fictional home.

character.bio: An Arctic fox who remembers where she put things, provided the entire ground has not changed overnight.

episode.subject: Arctic fox
episode.title: White fur, dark stones
episode.body:
My coat had begun coming loose in pale tufts. Rubbed against a rock and left a little of winter on its edge.

Underneath I was darker. The bare ground no longer made me look like something that had wandered into the wrong season.

Sat in a sunny patch and pulled at another loose tuft. It stuck to my lip. A great deal of looking appropriate involves looking ridiculous first.

media.subject: Arctic fox
media.detail: Arctic fox curled on bare gravel, with pale loose winter fur over its darker coat
media.creator: Jerzy Strzelecki

entries.sceneEvidence: Prior exact-hash review saw a curled fox on bare gravel with abundant loose pale fur over darker coat. Current Avatar06 full-image sheet reconfirms that broad scene, but is a screenshot, not a recovered exact source JPEG. The tuft on the lip is not established.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Vulpes lagopus source in Svalbard agrees with the coastal home and seasonal molt premise.

character.bio: A dumbo octopus who can leave any argument vertically, and usually does.

location.name: Deep Gulf of Mexico, approximate benthic home

episode.subject: dumbo octopus
episode.title: I stayed with the light
episode.body:
The light followed me. I went left. It went left. I stopped, and the enormous thing behind it stopped too.

I had tucked all my arms underneath me. Nothing down here had ever wanted such a thorough look. After a while I opened them a little. The thing held still.

Perhaps it was frightened. It had brought so much light.

I swam beside it until it began to rise. It was very slow, and kept looking back. I went a little way up with it, then turned toward the bottom.

For the rest of the night I kept checking behind me. I hope it found whatever it had come down here to find. It seemed terribly poorly equipped to be alone.

entries.sceneEvidence: Pale dumbo octopus suspended in black water under bright ROV illumination, arms curled into a conspicuous bundle. The visible light and posture support the encounter; companionship and nervousness remain fiction.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Grimpoteuthis at genus level, consistent with canon and a broadly defined deep Gulf home. Do not invent a species.

character.bio: A sea pig with exacting sediment preferences and a passenger he did not remember inviting.

location.name: Abyssal Pacific west of Monterey, approximate home

episode.subject: sea pig
episode.title: Something underneath
episode.body:
A small crab had tucked itself beneath me. I could feel the difference when it moved. At first I stopped every time, waiting for it to get off.

It stayed through three stops and one fairly pointed change of direction.

I resumed eating. The crab drew its legs closer underneath me and settled against my belly.

character.bio: A swimming sea cucumber who keeps discovering that her stomach comes with her.

location.name: Deep Caribbean south of Puerto Rico, approximate home

episode.subject: swimming sea cucumber
episode.title: A little mystery
episode.body: Someone said I should leave a little to the imagination. I tried turning sideways. My intestine came with me.

media.creator: NOAA Okeanos Explorer; color adjustment by Togabi

entries.taxonomyAndHome: Enypniastes eximia source at Puerto Rico agrees with the approximate Caribbean home. The prose addresses the reader without claiming eyesight.

character.bio: A leafy seadragon who resembles the garden and resents being treated as part of the gardening.

location.name: Seagrass and kelp near Rapid Bay

episode.subject: leafy seadragon underwater
episode.title: The open patch
episode.body: I crossed a gap between the weeds. All that careful resemblance and blue water behind me. I have never been more aware of the amount of myself on display.

entries.sceneEvidence: Golden leafy seadragon is conspicuous against open blue water, with weeds at the edges. That exposure directly supports the gap-between-weeds premise and camouflage embarrassment.
entries.taxonomyAndHome: Phycodurus eques; Kangaroo Island source and Rapid Bay fictional home are compatible southern Australian settings. The photo does not establish a journey between them.
